text: To go from chamber to chamber, and see no beauty; to find in the housemates no aim; to hear an endless chatter and blast; to be compelled to criticise; to hear only to dissent and to be disgusted; to find no invitation to what is good in us, and no receptacle for what is wise; this is a great price to pay for sweet bread and warm lodging.
author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
